title: Government Reputation and Fiscal Capacity
abstract: arXiv:2509.03087v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: How does uncertain implementation shape fiscal policy over time? We study an uninformed fiscal authority that chooses a distortionary tax-financed mandate and audit intensity while a privately informed executive decides whether to deliver or divert the proceeds. Reputation is the Bayesian state variable linking current fiscal control to future capacity. In a two-period benchmark, a mandate is also an experiment: delivery sacrifices current rents but preserves future access. We prove that the dynamic activation threshold is no greater than the square of the static reputation cutoff; the bound is exact and independent of discounting in a linear-benefit, quadratic-cost economy. A positive trial mandate may therefore be optimal when every positive tax is statically undesirable. In the infinite-horizon model, posterior reputation is a bounded martingale and its one-step conditional variance admits an exact policy-dependent formula. Zero m

translated_abstract: 摘要：不确定的实施如何随时间影响财政政策？我们研究了一个信息不足的财政当局，它选择一项扭曲性税收资助的任务和审计强度，而一个拥有私人信息的行政官员决定是交付还是挪用收益。声誉是贝叶斯状态变量，将当前的财政控制与未来的能力联系起来。在一个两期基准模型中，任务也是一种实验：交付牺牲当前租金但保留未来准入。我们证明，动态激活阈值不大于静态声誉截止点的平方；在线性收益、二次成本的经济中，该界限是精确的且与贴现无关。因此，当所有正税收在静态上不可取时，一个积极的试验性任务可能是最优的。在无限期模型下，后验声誉是一个有界鞅，其单步条件方差具有精确的策略依赖公式。零任务可能持续存在。
tldr: 本文揭示了在不确定实施下，政府声誉作为动态财政政策的关键驱动因素，并证明了动态激活阈值与静态声誉截止点的精确平方关系，以及试验性任务在特定条件下可优化财政能力。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that government reputation is a key driver of dynamic fiscal policy under uncertain implementation, proves an exact squared relationship between dynamic activation thresholds and static reputation cutoffs, and shows that trial mandates can optimize fiscal capacity under certain conditions.
